title: Distinct Feedback-Strength Requirements for Quantum-State Ensemble Preparation under Channel-Equivalent Monitoring
authors: Haitao Huang, Qinglin Zhao, Xiaoyu Li
abstract: Different measurements of the same environment can preserve the average quantum channel yet change the feedback strength needed to prepare a state ensemble. We establish this distinction for a multiqubit register under complete Pauli monitoring, targeting the uniform ensemble of real-amplitude pure states. With unit detection efficiency, public records, and bounded Hamiltonian feedback, fixed transverse noise requires a minimum peak strength proportional to $ε^{-1}$ at distributional error $ε$. Tangent noise instead admits a construction requiring only $O[\sqrt{\log(1/ε)}]$. At fixed preparation time, we determine the optimum over all allowed feedback policies and derive a geometric lower bound beyond radial symmetry. The separation identifies the measurement realization as part of the control-resource specification for monitored ensemble preparation.
summary: This theoretical work distinguishes the resource requirements for preparing a quantum state ensemble based on the specific measurement readout used, even if the overall average channel is the same. It proves a dramatic separation in required feedback strength between different monitoring types. This highlights that the measurement process itself dictates the necessary control resources for high-fidelity quantum state preparation.
main_problem: The paper investigates the distinct resource costs (feedback strength) required to prepare a target quantum state ensemble when continuous monitoring is performed, even if the average quantum channel remains unchanged.
main_result: A significant separation is established: preparing the ensemble under fixed transverse noise requires a strength scaling of $\Theta(\epsilon^{-1})$, whereas tangent noise requires only $O(\sqrt{\log(1/\epsilon)})$, proving measurement realization is part of the control specification.
method: The analysis uses the trace-Wasserstein distance to quantify ensemble error and compares resource costs derived from different monitoring regimes (e.g., tangent vs. transverse monitoring).
model_or_system: The model is a multiqubit register undergoing continuous monitoring and feedback control, targeting the uniform ensemble of real-amplitude pure states.
key_observables: Terminal ensemble error ($\epsilon$), required Hamiltonian strength ($U$), and the feedback strength parameter ($\delta$).
important_parameters: The separation is quantified by comparing $C_{d,\delta}(\epsilon)$ for $\delta>0$ versus $\delta=0$.
main_assumptions: Assumes unit detection efficiency and bounded Hamiltonian feedback; the tangent construction provides an upper bound, but a matching lower bound is noted as open.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the scaling difference in required feedback strength between different monitoring scenarios (e.g., sustained vs. normal feedback).
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem by comparing monitoring types, derives lower bounds using Wasserstein distance, and culminates in a theorem quantifying the distinct resource scaling based on the measurement readout realization.
why_interesting: It provides fundamental theoretical bounds on the resources needed for quantum control under measurement, which is crucial for understanding realistic quantum feedback protocols in quantum optics and open quantum systems.
